title: Projective curve jet flags and their actual Hilbert weight coefficients
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $r=n+2\ge2$, and let $i:X\to\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Use $D=X_{\mathrm{red}}$ and its canonical immersion [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], and use the genuine component normalizations, branch germs and tangent-line equations of [def-sfb-projective-curve-branch-data]. The linear forms, weighted flags, monomial bases, section modules and minimum weights are those of [def-sfb-weighted-monomial-basis-weight]. Define the following predicates and concrete section map. A family $\rho_m$ is polynomial restriction when its value on every standard chart is the dehomogenized polynomial times the standard generator of $i^*\mathcal O(m)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-pc-module-pullback]. A rational number $a$ is its leading weight coefficient for $(b,w)$ when monomial bases exist eventually and $|w_{\rho,b,w}(m)-am^2|\le Am$ eventually for some $A\in\mathbf N$. The coefficient vector of a linear form is its degree-one monomial coefficients. A form vanishes at a point when its germ divided by every nonvanishing coordinate lies in the maximal ideal. It has branch order at least $h$ when the corresponding branch germ belongs to $\mathfrak m_q^h$; this includes zero germs. Define the linear-section map by pulling back the standard coordinate sections of $\mathcal O(1)$ by the canonical tensor-pullback unit and taking their coefficient linear combination. An embedded component $j:Y\to\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ is rational normal in its own span when $Y\cong\mathbf P^1_k$ over $k$ and this map is surjective onto $H^0(Y,j^*\mathcal O(1))$; equivalently its embedding in its span is the complete degree-$e$ embedding, where $e$ is its hyperplane degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. The point flag has weights at most one and zero-weight subspace exactly the forms vanishing at the point. The ramified branch flag has weights at most four, subspaces at thresholds $0,1,2$ exactly branch orders at least $4,3,2$, and the threshold-three subspace equals the threshold-two subspace. The tangent flag has weights at most two, zero-weight subspace the tangent-line equations, and threshold-one subspace the point equations. Empty graded pieces are allowed; all weights are natural numbers.
